/start: Opens the current character’s Default/Alternate opening message chooser once after /new or /reset. Selecting a greeting commits it and starts the standard session. An already started session cannot start again. Before that, ordinary dialogue and conversational media return “Please use /start command.” without a story-model call or transcript entry. Setup is /character; /start performs no readiness-model probe. Plain “start” is no longer an alias. In Light Novel mode, the greeting immediately schedules its first 3–4 action choices. If delivery of the committed greeting fails, retry its existing selection to re-deliver the same opening, not a new one.
/help: Opens this guide. Pick a category, then tap a command to see what it does and what it changes.
/cancel: Cancels the current scoped input step, such as session naming, memory input, image prompts, settings, or other panel-driven text entry. Nothing is applied; the pending input is cleared safely.
/status: Shows a formatted read-only session status message directly in Telegram.
/usage: Sends a plain-text, read-only token usage summary for the active session in this chat or Forum Topic over the last 7 days. Shows input, output, total, cached and reasoning tokens; reported/complete coverage, failed/cancelled calls, daily UTC totals, and up to five top models and purposes. Missing counters are unknown, not zero; partially reported totals may be incomplete. Cached and reasoning tokens are subsets, not extra tokens. Reads the existing local ledger without calling a model or opening a Mini App or inline panel. Provider-reported usage is not a billing statement, price estimate or remaining quota.
/new: Asks for a name (1–80 characters), then creates and activates a fresh isolated session. Opening this flow closes your previous unclosed management panel in the same chat/topic, but preserves the previous session's Telegram conversation and stored history. The new standard session requires /start before conversation. Send /cancel during naming to leave without creating an empty session.
/reset: Opens a confirmation panel. Confirming clears only the active session's transcript, Hindsight documents, variants, continuity/curated/episodic memory, NPC Bank state and pending story choices, and best-effort deletes the bridge's tracked Telegram user inputs, assistant replies, and Light Novel choice/selection messages for that session. Character, Normal/Light Novel mode, A/B/C strategy, Persona, World and System Prompt remain configured. Telegram deletion failures never undo the durable reset; other sessions and topics are unchanged. The standard session returns to unstarted; use /start to choose the opening greeting again.
/session: Lets you switch between sessions, create new ones, or delete inactive ones. Deleting a session removes its SQLite data and queues session-scoped Hindsight cleanup, which retries in the background even while memory is off. Active or busy sessions can't be deleted.
/sync: Opens Live API Sync for this session. It talks to SillyTavern's local API — no chat files or JSONL transfers. Toggle realtime to do an initial reconciliation before turning on background sync. Sync now runs a one-shot API reconciliation even when background realtime is off; Refresh status only redraws state. If there's a sync-ID mismatch, initial divergence, two-sided edits, or oversized API records, sync stops instead of guessing. Credentials stay separate from Telegram.
/update: Checks a stable GitHub release and binds confirmation to the displayed version. Installation requires a clean main checkout, an SSH-signed annotated tag trusted by an independently installed allowed-signers file, and a safe managed live mirror. It verifies and stages before activation. Changed runtime dependencies require manual installation. Restart failures are reported explicitly; session data and private configuration are not copied or reset.
/providers: Opens the provider/model controls and first shows the active session's Story and Utility models plus their independent reasoning budgets. Choose either model or configure Story and Utility reasoning (None/Low/Medium/High/Max/Custom). Both budgets are session-scoped. Story reasoning applies to Story-model replies; Utility reasoning applies to Utility-model tasks such as summaries, curated memory, scene state, Light Novel strategy B choices, and character rank/optimizer work. Provider health and Refresh provider catalog remain available in the provider list.
/character: Opens native character cards with ranked name buttons and character actions. Selecting a card starts the standard-session setup wizard: Normal/Light Novel → A/B/C only for Light Novel → Persona → World → System Prompt → Session → Apply. Selections remain temporary and actor-scoped until final Apply; choose an unstarted session or create a new one. Then use /start. The Info, Optimizer, Upload and protected Delete actions remain available. Rank icons appear in the main, Info and Optimizer pickers, with the current session character marked ✅; selected Info and Optimizer details show the rank label or an unranked dash. Optimizer supports Manual Suggestion followed by cumulative Revise previews and reranks after Apply. Existing group setup is unchanged.
/persona: Opens native SillyTavern Persona controls. Choose, create, edit, or disable a Persona — all stored in settings.json and the native User Avatars folder. The review panel shows the description in Telegram's copyable code block. Delete only targets inactive, unreferenced Personas — the active one and any used by other sessions are protected.
/world: Opens World Info selection. You can activate multiple JSON lorebooks at the same time — they're validated and merged at prompt time. Use Upload World JSON to add a native World Info file, or the trash button to delete an inactive file. Active or referenced files are protected.
/note: Opens the Author's Note panel. Off clears it. User input waits for your next scoped text message and uses it as the note.
/systemprompt: Opens the native JSON/TXT System Prompt picker. The prompt body stays private — it's applied during generation, but menus and /status only show the label.
/language: Opens per-session reply language controls. Auto follows whatever language you're writing in. A fixed language adds a final render pass to every response so it comes out in that language — streaming preview is disabled in fixed mode so you only see the final output.
/expression: Opens character expression controls for this session. Automatic mode reads the model's reply, classifies the emotion locally, and sends a native sprite only when the expression actually changes. Manual mode lets you pick a sprite directly. If no matching sprite exists, it falls back to neutral, then the avatar, then text-only.
/imagine: Open the image panel. Choose Realism or Anime, then Current Scene to prepare a visual prompt with Utility, or Custom Prompt to enter your own description. The checkmark shows the session's saved style; Realism is the default. Both styles work with text generation and character references when the selected model supports them. Options selects image model and size; Reset restores default model, Square and Realism. Custom Prompt displays the available input length after reserving style and reference instructions. Successful delivery contains only the image. Generation leaves the story transcript unchanged.
/settings: Opens generation settings for this session. Edit temperature, max tokens, top P, frequency penalty, presence penalty, or stop sequences. Story and Utility reasoning are configured under /providers. Humanizer and Grounded User are independent ON/OFF toggles; both are off by default. Grounded User keeps abilities, success and NPC/world reactions tied to established story facts without erasing explicit Persona advantages.
/stream: Opens the streaming on/off panel for this chat. Choose a button to apply the state. Typed forms such as /stream on and /stream off are accepted for compatibility with the command router but deliberately open the same panel rather than silently changing state. Token-limit auto-continuation stays cumulative, cancellable, and bounded.
/preset: Opens preset controls. Apply, save, or delete validated generation setting presets — all from the panel.
/macro: Opens a panel, then waits for one text message to preview supported SillyTavern macros. Send /cancel to leave without running anything.
/macro <text>: Expands supported SillyTavern macros immediately against the supplied text and returns the preview without changing the transcript.
/stscript: Opens the allowlisted STscript panel. Only safe bridge actions are exposed — no shell commands, no filesystem access, no network requests. Reset goes through the normal session confirmation flow.
/regen: Generates a fresh response variant for your latest user turn. The previous variant is kept — use /swipe to browse them.
/swipe: Opens stored response variants for the latest turn. Browse through them and keep the one you like best.
/branch: Opens the response branch selector for the active session.
/continue: Continues the latest assistant response from where it left off. When a streaming provider hits its output token limit, the bridge can automatically continue with up to three bounded continuation requests while keeping the live preview cumulative; use /continue when you deliberately want another segment after that.
/edit: Opens a panel, then waits for replacement text for your latest user message. Send /cancel to leave it unchanged. The response is regenerated from the edited text.
/edit <text>: Replaces the latest user turn immediately with the supplied text and regenerates the assistant response. The operation uses the same session-scoped edit/recovery path as the panel form.
/retry: Retries the latest failed character response. It replays the original message without creating a duplicate committed turn — clean recovery after a crash or timeout.
/prompt: Opens the read-only prompt inspector with sections for budget, memory/RAG, and group context. Prompt diagnostics stay on this panel.
/memory: Opens Hindsight memory controls. You can turn memory on or off and search within the active session. Recall is always session-scoped — it never pulls in memories from other sessions, users, or characters.
/memory search <query>: Searches Hindsight memory for <query> within the active session and returns up to five matching remembered facts. Recall stays strictly session-scoped, so results never come from another session.
/memory curated: Opens the curated-memory panel to view durable distilled facts or refresh them with the Utility model. Refresh stays on the panel and memory must be enabled.
/npc: Opens the active session's persistent NPC Bank. Browse supporting-character dossiers and visible structured fields, review field history, refresh state with the bounded Utility-model extractor, and undo only the latest visible field revision. Restricted fields respect the active character's known_by audience, and stale undo confirmations are refused if the field changed after review.
/remember: Opens a panel, then waits for one explicit long-term fact to store in Hindsight. Send /cancel to leave without storing anything.
/remember <fact>: Stores one explicit fact immediately in active-session Hindsight memory. The fact is bounded and session-scoped; it is never written to another session.
/summarize: Opens a confirmation panel before regenerating the active-session summary from its stored conversation and current memory context. The resulting summary remains scoped to this session and is used as continuity context when older turns are compacted.
/databank: Opens Data Bank RAG controls for status, documents, search, versions, activation, removal, and reindexing. These actions are panel-driven.
/voice: Opens automatic quote-driven TTS controls. Use the panel buttons to turn it on or off. When enabled, dialogue in straight double quotes can be synthesized from both user and character messages; narration and unquoted text stay silent. Typed /voice on or /voice off also opens the panel rather than changing state silently.
/voice_input: Opens voice-input transcription controls for enablement, STT model, and language. Use the panel to apply changes; typed on/off/status/model forms route to the same controls.
/voice_input language: Opens the STT language panel. Auto detects from the audio, a fixed code forces one language, and User input asks you each time.
/group: Only works inside a Telegram Forum Topic. Opens the topic-local group panel for members, speaker, mode, enable/disable, turn controls, and new group sessions.
/group goal: Opens the hidden, session-local Director objective panel for this Forum Topic group. Use the panel to set, review, or clear the objective without adding it to the transcript.
/scene: Opens the active session's structured scene-state panel. Use its Refresh and Clear controls; typed scene subcommands route back to this same panel.
/lightnovel: Dedicated session-scoped Normal/Light Novel control, not part of /settings. Before /start, choose A — Story Inline (story and choices together), B — Utility Model (story then utility choices), C — Story Second Pass (story then another story-model call), or Normal. Started sessions show status and restore their current choices; use /new or /reset before changing mode. Light Novel offers a random 3–4 distinct actions after the opening greeting and each story turn. The panel message shows every action in full with numbered labels, while compact 1–4 selector buttons avoid truncated Telegram button labels. A permanent ⏭ Next Scene button advances the narrative without speaking, deciding, or acting for the user character until that character can meaningfully participate again. Click once to submit the exact stored action through the normal durable user-turn pipeline, or type a reply to invalidate old choices. Count and ready choices survive restarts. After a generated choice or Next Scene is selected, the old panel becomes a Telegram block quote of the visible choice label with no “Selected:” prefix; the durable submitted text is unchanged. Mode A automatically repairs missing or invalid inline choices with one durable choice-only Story-model pass while preserving the committed story; Retry Choices appears only if that automatic recovery fails. Retry Choices retries only choice generation, never the committed story. This first version supports standard sessions; group orchestration is unchanged.
/narrative: Choose Player-centric, Ensemble, World-driven, or Observer for the current story. Advanced controls change point of view, your role, scene focus, off-screen scenes, and user control. Your dialogue, thoughts, commitments, and important decisions remain yours. Save as my default prefills future /character setup; it never changes an existing session. I am not MC remains a separate setting.
/director: Open the hidden Director Room to inspect the current scene, thread, accepted plan and recent decisions. Reassess uses the Director model, which inherits Utility then Story when unset. Choose a one-scene direction or a persistent objective; your dialogue and consequential decisions remain yours. Thread selection changes a future plan, never committed history.
/check: Open the session action-check panel. Auto uses Utility and is the default; Director uses the configured Director route; Manual disables automatic adjudication. Mode buttons edit the same panel. Manual Check shows the explicit /check syntax and Recent Checks reads saved local receipts without a model call.
/check <domain> <DC> <action>: Use /check stealth 12 cross the courtyard. The bridge records one d20 roll plus established skill/item/condition modifiers. DC must be 1–20. Send your next story turn to narrate the consequences. Delivery retries preserve the same result; each new /check is a new action. Checks do not advance NPC agenda timers. Editing, resetting or replacing the action invalidates its check.
/trackers: View saved story trackers and recent d20 checks for the active session. The view includes visible relationships, agendas, inventory, skills, conditions, factions and linked quests and user tasks, plus saved-source freshness. It reads canonical SQLite state without a model request, a new roll, or a story turn. Private intelligence and future payoffs are omitted. Open Mini App Manage → Story trackers for the fuller list. /status continues to show session configuration.
